conclusion: Halving native student-output thresholds recruits MBON04 and preserves useful A feeding, but removes A-period student dopamine recruitment. The output-specific dry-probe intervention tests whether MBON04 inhibition causes that lost teacher response. This preparation has not established learned B behavior. Student viability and teacher efficacy must coexist in the recurrent circuit; each isolated gain fix is insufficient.
